A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StreetUnveiler. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the expanded evaluation and revised layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original Waymo experiments, quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–3, and qualitative reconstruction, semantic-label and mesh results.

after.justification: v3 reports original Waymo and PandaSet experiments, additional baseline comparisons, computational measurements and quantitative geometry evaluation in Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: Equation 8 changes the reported shrinking loss from summed opacity to mean opacity, dividing by the number of Gaussians while retaining its weight of 0.001. The core hard-label 2DGS, alpha-mask generation, time-reversal inpainting and re-optimization pipeline remains.

E1.justification: v3 extends the Waymo-only evaluation to nine PandaSet street scenes, adding an independent driving dataset to the main comparisons and ablations. The task remains street unveiling; PandaSet's stated 360-degree sensor coverage does not establish surrounding-camera evaluation, since v3 specifies frontal sequences.

E2.justification: v3 adds an adapted LeftRefill comparator in Table 4 and evaluates StreetSurf for geometry in Table 7. These introduce direct comparisons with the inpainting backbone and a surface-reconstruction method, respectively. Both were cited in v1 but were not evaluated as these comparators; the original main comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: v3 revises the FID procedure from v1's stated framewise computation and averaging to comparison of image collections. It also introduces geometry evaluation using LiDAR, a 5-meter mesh-cropping rule, Chamfer Distance and F-score at 0.25 meters, plus timing protocols averaging eight scenes per dataset. These are substantive reported protocol additions and revisions, without establishing whether existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds stagewise computational profiling, segmentation-boundary failure cases, and analysis of naive LeftRefill failures when future references omit relevant regions. These investigate efficiency and failure mechanisms beyond v1's analyses. The time-forward comparison is retained and extended, not newly introduced: it already appeared in v1 Appendix B.1 and Table 3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. v3's averages over scenes and runtime measurements do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 replace the reported Waymo values: StreetUnveiler's LPIPS/FID changes from 0.241/157.970 to 0.216/127.581. v3 adds PandaSet results of 0.261/155.527 and new LeftRefill, runtime and geometry results. These are revised or additional estimates, not established same-setting gains. Both versions' Table 1 values give SDXL the lowest FID, despite their misleading accompanying wording.

T1.justification: Equation 8 revises the mathematical definition of the opacity penalty from a sum to an average and defines the Gaussian count N. This is a limited, non-equivalent normalization change. The remaining mathematical framework is retained, and neither version introduces theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: hard-label semantic 2DGS, alpha-based identification of unobservable regions, and time-reversal inpainting for reconstructing empty streets. Additional evaluation and the new 'A Simple Baseline' subtitle do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion: it explicitly limits consistency guarantees to forward-facing cameras, discusses dynamic-object handling and segmentation failures, and interprets reconstruction cost and SDF-versus-TSDF geometry differences. v1's standalone limitations list is replaced; its explicit linear-cost and pretrained-inpainter bottleneck caveats are no longer stated in that form.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies the A40 GPU, frontal-camera selection, 24 Waymo and nine PandaSet scenes, label inheritance during densification, and restriction of re-optimization to nearby Gaussians. It also documents new baseline settings, geometry preprocessing, runtime measurements and supplementary-video access paths. Newly specifying local re-optimization does not establish that its implementation changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Reffusion, Inpaint3D, InstantSplat and S3Gaussian, and develops distinctions from StreetSurf and dynamic/static scene decomposition. The principal related-work organization and street-unveiling positioning remain. Publication updates to existing references do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: v3 adds the subtitle, updates affiliations and publication text, edits terminology and sentences, and expands the appendix into additional-results and thematic-discussion sections. Most main-text prose and the principal section sequence remain, so this is limited editing and reorganization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns Tables 1–3 with dataset-specific columns, merges the main ablation presentation and redisplays the existing time-order comparison there. It adds Tables 4–7 and figures for LeftRefill, geometry accuracy, segmentation failures and additional examples. The conference template also changes layout; earlier semantic, geometry and mesh figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's Waymo results and qualitative geometry: PandaSet tests broader applicability, the LeftRefill comparison helps assess the pipeline's added value, and geometry and runtime measurements address previously unquantified properties. Explicit camera and segmentation limitations improve interpretation. Geometry validation still concerns scenes before removal, and PandaSet timings are not reconciled between Tables 5 and 6 (311 seconds for 80 frames versus 5.09 seconds per frame). These reporting limitations do not outweigh the stronger empirical support and clearer applicability boundaries.
